items.title: How would you find early users for an AI trading assistant before MVP?
items.raw_excerpt: I’m building an AI analyst desk for retail FX traders. The idea is to split the work of a real FX analyst desk across five LLM agents: macro context, setup comparison, risk review, specialist synthesis, and reflection/audit. The product generates structured market reports that traders can use before making their own decisions. A report may include macro context, strategy candidates, risk notes, entry/SL/TP zones, invalidation conditions, and a suggested position idea. It does not custody user funds, and the current direction is decision support, not auto-execution. The hard part is trust. The MVP is not fully finished yet, and in trading/finance it is very difficult to get people to try a new product without credibility. But to make the product trustworthy, I need feedback from real users.

items.title: AgentWing – make AI agents complete tasks faster
items.raw_excerpt: Hi HN, I’m building AgentWing. The idea is simple: AI agents usually execute work as one long sequence: plan → act → wait → observe → act again → verify → finish That makes agent workflows feel slow, especially when parts of the task do not actually depend on each other. AgentWing adds a director layer that turns one agent task into multiple isolated worker runs. excerpt_i18n.en: On May 20, the 2026 "ByteDance Scholarship" officially opened for applications. The scholarship targets university students in cutting-edge technology fields, offering a cash reward of up to 300,000 RMB per awardee and their advisor. This year, the program has expanded its application scope to universities worldwide for the first time, and the number of awardees will exceed last year's 20 recipients. According to reports, the ByteDance Scholarship was launched in 2021, aiming to incentivize the most promising young researchers in technology to "explore the frontiers of intelligence in uncharted territories," thereby advancing research and applications in artificial intelligence. The award expects candidates to have innovative ideas, practical achievements, or be exploring solutions to long-term valuable problems in fields such as artificial intelligence, computer science and technology, and basic sciences. Even if research is ongoing, candidates can submit applications based on interim results. Over the six years since its inception, ByteDance has continuously increased its investment in the program: the number of awardees has grown from 10 in the first year to over 20; the selection scope has expanded from mainland China to universities worldwide; the individual research incentive for awardees has increased from 100,000 RMB to 200,000 RMB, which can be freely used for research needs. Additionally, the program pioneered a 100,000 RMB advisor bonus in the industry to recognize advisors' contributions to talent cultivation. Beyond financial support, the ByteDance Scholarship also focuses on broadening the academic horizons of young scholars. Awardees will be invited to join the ByteScholars research community, engaging in regular exchanges with renowned scholars, industry experts, and past recipients. Many previous awardees have noted that the scholarship has significantly enhanced their academic perspectives.

excerpt_i18n.en: In recent years, the lifelines of U.S. AI giants have seemed tightly held by Nvidia, until Cerebras stepped into the spotlight with its $67 billion market cap. Last night Beijing time, an American company selling "big chips"—Cerebras—made a stellar debut on Nasdaq: its closing price surged 68% above the IPO price, reaching a total market value of $67 billion. "This is the largest IPO so far this year and also sets a record for the listing of a 'pure AI chip company' in U.S. stock market history," said Zhang Lin, an analyst who has long tracked U.S. hardware stocks, to Leiphone. On the surface, this is a high-tech wealth-creating IPO; but in the eyes of Silicon Valley's core circle, it feels more like the starting gun for an impending "computing power reshuffle." "Cerebras's listing means that non-GPU paths can not only survive but also command astonishing premiums," Zhang Lin noted. The chip industry has begun to move away from the single-choice era of "buying cards and paying taxes," with differentiated architectures truly emerging. Moreover, according to computing power industry investor Wang Ning, this IPO is also, to some extent, shifting the power landscape of the U.S. AI camp. Behind Cerebras stand giants eager to redefine the power hierarchy of the AI era. "This is not just a simple listing, but a 'chip catfish' officially entering the game, triggering a 'critical moment' in the global AI industry's discourse power struggle," Wang Ning emphasized. For more intriguing insights, feel free to add the author's WeChat.

UU. parecía estar en manos de Nvidia, hasta que Cerebras apareció en el foco con una valoración de 67 000 millones de dólares. Ayer, hora de Pekín, una empresa estadounidense que vende "chips grandes", Cerebras, debutó en el Nasdaq con un rendimiento excepcional: su precio de cierre subió un 68 % respecto al precio de emisión, alcanzando una capitalización de mercado total de 67 000 millones de dólares. "Esta es la OPI más grande del año hasta la fecha y también establece un récord en la historia del mercado de valores de EE. UU. para la cotización de una 'empresa pura de chips de IA'", comentó Zhang Lin, analista que sigue de cerca los activos de hardware en el mercado estadounidense, a Leiphone.
